title: tenant-provisioning-and-evidence-package-playbook-2026
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines a standardized, auditable zero-touch tenant provisioning and evidence package process for Redwood Private VPC and on-prem deployments. It consolidates deployment-preflight checks, automated acceptance tests, evidence artifacts for compliance, and day-2 verification steps. The objective is to reduce field friction, ensure consistent SLA posture, and create a repeatable evidence bundle for Security & Compliance reviews.

Scope
-----
- Tenant onboarding on VPC-based private deployments and single-site on-prem appliances.
- Applies to both self-service provisioning and operator-assisted onboarding.
- Includes the acceptance test suite, required observability contracts, and the evidence package format expected by compliance.

Definitions
-----------
- Tenant: customer logical isolation (namespace + billing/accounting).
- Provisioning bundle: automated artifacts used to instantiate tenant resources (manifest, keys, quotas).
- Evidence package: zipped set of artifacts demonstrating controls and successful acceptance tests.

Prerequisites (operator/customer)
--------------------------------
- Operator account with RBAC role: redwood-tenant-admin.
- Customer-provided: CIDR blocks for tenant VPC, BGP ASN (if using cross-connect), KMS key ARN for encryption-at-rest, list of authorized egress endpoints.
- Minimum hardware (on-prem): 2x inference nodes (A100/4090 class), 3x control-plane VMs, 1x NFS/S3-compatible storage for artifacts.

Hardware & Network Matrix (minimum)
----------------------------------
| Component | Minimum | Ports/Protocols |
|-----------|---------|-----------------|
| Control-plane VM | 3 x t3.large equiv | 443/TLS, 9000/metrics (prometheus), 5671/queue (AMQP) |
| Inference node | 2 x GPU nodes (>=48GB GPU mem) | 22/ssh, 5555/kvcache, 8080/runtime-api |
| Storage | S3-compatible (10 TB) | 443/TLS |
| KMS/HSM | Customer-managed KMS | 443/TLS |
| Interconnect | 1 Gbps redundant | BGP/ECMP if applicable |

Note: For small proof-of-concepts a single inference node is acceptable, but SLA must be adjusted.

Zero-Touch Provisioning Flow (high level)
----------------------------------------
1. Customer submits tenant request via API or portal with required fields: tenant-name, email, vpc-cidr, kms_key_arn, allowed-egress-list.
2. Provisioning service validates request against the Customer Readiness Policy (CIDR overlap, ASN conflicts, quota limits).
3. Provisioning service generates a tenant manifest and signs it with operator enclave key.
4. If VPC mode: automation creates VPC peer, route table entries, and security groups per network template.
5. If on-prem mode: operator uploads signed manifest and triggers field-operator deployment via the Operator Console; appliance performs a signed manifest verify.
6. Automated acceptance test job executes (see Acceptance Test Suite).
7. On success, evidence package is assembled and delivered to the customer and compliance buckets. On failure, automated rollback hooks run (see Rollback section).

Provisioning API example
------------------------
curl -X POST https://provisioning.redwood.internal/v1/tenants
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <operator-token>"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{\n    "tenant_name":"acme-inc-east-1",\n    "contact_email":"ops@acme.example.com",\n    "vpc_cidr":"10.40.0.0/16",\n    "kms_key_arn":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abc-123",\n    "egress_allowlist":["api.acme.example.com:443"],\n    "quota": {"concurrent_gpus":4, "max_rps":1000}\n  }'

Acceptance Test Suite (automated)
--------------------------------
Purpose: validate functional correctness and compliance controls before marking tenant ACTIVE. Tests must be runnable unattended.

Core tests (order):
- Network reachability: verify control plane <-> inference nodes (TCP/8080), KV cache connectivity, and egress allowlist enforcement.
- Runtime sanity: POST a sample prompt to runtime API and assert 200 + token streaming.
- Performance smoke: generate 100 short requests across 1 minute and verify p95 latency < 200ms for cold-start disabled profiles.
- KV-cache warmup: ensure KV cache populated and subsequent request latency improves > 20% for repetitive prefix.
- Telemetry ingestion: confirm that control-plane metrics are visible in central telemetry (prometheus labels tenant=<tenant-name>).
- Encryption at rest: check model artifact S3 objects are encrypted with provided KMS key.

Examples (commands)
-------------------
# Network check (from operator host)
curl -sSf https://10.40.2.10:8080/health || exit 1
# Runtime request (scripted)
curl -s -X POST https://runtime.tenant.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>" -d '{"input":"Hello"}' | jq '.status'

Pass criteria: all core tests must return green. Failures must produce a diagnostic bundle (see Evidence Package).

Evidence Package Format
-----------------------
When provisioning completes (success or failure), the system must produce a signed evidence package containing:
- tenant-manifest.json (signed)
- provisioning-log.txt (timestamped events)
- acceptance-test-report.json (structured pass/fail + artifacts)
- config-diff.patch (before/after network & quota changes)
- telemetry-screenshot.png (png of tenant metrics dashboard)
- artifacts-checksums.txt (sha256s)

The evidence package must be stored in the operator S3 bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/<tenant>/<timestamp>-evidence.zip and a copy placed in customer-provided evidence location if configured.

Upgrade & Rollback Considerations for New Tenants
-------------------------------------------------
- Default provisioning uses model-image pinned tags (no floating latest) to avoid surprise model changes.
- If an operator-side runtime upgrade is in progress, provisioning must be shunted to a compatibility pool; see compatibility labels: runtime.compatible=[true|false].
- Rollback hook (on acceptance failure): automatically decommission created resources in the reverse order of creation and mark the tenant state as REQUIRES_ATTENTION. Keep the evidence package for forensic analysis.

Observability & Day-2 Checks (post-provision)
---------------------------------------------
- SLOs to monitor for tenant health:
  - availability: 99.95% monthly
  - 95th percentile token latency: < 150ms for standard profiles
  - error rate: < 0.5% 1m window
- Required telemetry tags: tenant_id, tenant_name, region, model_variant, provisioning_id.
- Day-2 automated checks (daily): storage encryption audit, KMS key rotation window check, telemetry heartbeat (last 5 minutes), resource entitlement vs usage (quota drifting).

Operator Runbook (quick actions)
-------------------------------
1. If acceptance test fails: open incident with tag: onboarding-failure, attach evidence package.
2. For transient network failures: trigger re-run of acceptance tests via: 
   curl -X POST https://provisioning.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/<tenant>/rerun-tests
3. For stuck provisioning (progress > 10 min stalled): escalate to platform-engineering and run safe-decommission: 
   provisionctl decommission --tenant <tenant> --preserve-evidence false

Appendix: sample tenant-manifest.yaml
------------------------------------
```yaml
tenant_name: acme-inc-east-1
contact_email: ops@acme.example.com
vpc:
  cidr: "10.40.0.0/16"
  route_table: auto
kms_key_arn: "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abc-123"
quotas:
  concurrent_gpus: 4
  max_rps: 1000
egress_allowlist:
  - "api.acme.example.com:443"
signed_by: "operator-enclave-2026"
signature: "<base64-signature>"
```

-------------------------------------------------------

  "tenant": "acme-inc-east-1",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-01T15:04:05Z",
  "results": [
    {"test":"network_reachability","status":"pass","detail":"tcp 8080 ok"},
    {"test":"runtime_smoke","status":"pass","latency_ms":78},

  ]
}
